Predict class membership or outcomes from a fitted model, and simulate data from it

Source: R/mixture-regression-predict.R, R/predict-docs.R, R/predict.R
latents-predict.Rd

predict() applies a fitted model to the original sample or new observations to obtain class membership probabilities or predicted outcomes.

For latent profile and class models, it estimates each observation's probability of belonging to each class, given its observed indicators, and identifies the most probable class. These probabilities express uncertainty in classification; the assigned class provides a discrete summary of that uncertainty.

For mixture regression models, it predicts outcomes from the relationships estimated within each class, either separately by class or averaged over class membership probabilities. Growth mixture models also provide individual trajectories informed by the person's observed outcomes.

simulate() generates replicate outcomes under a fitted mixture regression or growth mixture model, preserving the original predictors and grouping structure. The simulations reflect the model's assumed variation in class membership and outcomes while holding the estimated parameters fixed.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'latents_mixture_regression'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("response", "class_response", "posterior", "probabilities"),
  ...,
  trials = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'latents_mixture_regression'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, type = c("class", "posterior", "density"), ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted model with a prediction method:

  • a profile or class model from lpa(), lca(), multilpa() or multilca() without membership covariates;

  • a mixture regression from mixture_regression();

  • a growth mixture (mixture_regression(random = )).

A membership-covariate fit and an lta() fit raise latents_unsupported_prediction; the additive, dispersion and cross-level families of multilpa() have no predict() method. simulate() takes a mixture regression or a growth mixture only.

newdata

NULL (default) for the fitted rows, or a data frame with the indicator or predictor columns (and id and membership covariates where the model uses them).

type

What to predict. The first value listed for each kind of model is its default.

For a profile or class model:

  • "class" (default): each row's most probable profile and its posterior probability, and in a two-level model the group's most probable group class and its posterior probability;

  • "posterior": the same, plus the posterior probability of every profile;

  • "density": each row's log density under the fitted model, marginal over profiles and group classes, for scoring or a held-out likelihood.

For a mixture regression:

  • "response" (default): the mean outcome averaged over the classes with their prior probabilities (expected successes for a binomial count response);

  • "class_response": the mean outcome under each class, one row per observation and class;

  • "posterior": each row's class probabilities given its outcome, which newdata must contain, and the most probable class;

  • "probabilities": the probability of each outcome category under each class; ordinal family only.

For a growth mixture:

  • "response" (default): the class mean trajectories averaged with each person's prior class probabilities;

  • "class_response": each class's mean trajectory, with random effects set to zero, one row per observation and class;

  • "posterior": each person's class probabilities given the observed outcomes, one row per person;

  • "class_conditional": one row per observation and class: the class trajectory plus the person's random effects predicted under that class, E(b | y, class);

  • "conditional": the "class_conditional" trajectories averaged with the posterior class probabilities, one row per observation;

  • "random_effects": the predicted random effects, one row per person and class with its posterior probability; their posterior-weighted mean is lcmm::predictRE().

The last four use the outcomes, which newdata must then contain.

...

Unused. A profile, class or growth mixture predict() warns with latents_unused_argument for an argument it does not take.

trials

For binomial mixture-regression predictions, the number of trials: one non-negative whole number, a vector with one value per row, or a column name in the prediction data. NULL uses the fitted trials when newdata = NULL, or infers them from the response columns when present. A count response otherwise requires trials; a Bernoulli fit defaults to one trial. For type = "posterior", any explicit value must agree with the observed response. Predictions remain on the expected success-count scale; trials = 1 requests probabilities for each trial.

nsim

Number of simulated outcome vectors (default 1).

seed

NULL (default) uses and advances the caller's random stream. An integer makes the simulation reproducible and restores the caller's .Random.seed. R does not store the cached Box-Muller normal draw in .Random.seed, so the next normal draw is not preserved when that generator has a cached draw.

Value

A base data.frame. Its rows and columns depend on the model and type; row is the row's position in newdata (or in the fitted data).

Profile or class model, one row per row of the data:

  • "class": row, the group identifier (two-level models), profile (the most probable profile; 0 for the noise component), posterior (its probability) and, with more than one group class, group_class and group_posterior;

  • "posterior": the same, plus probability_profile_1, probability_profile_2 and so on;

  • "density": row and log_density.

Mixture regression:

  • "response": row and fitted, one row per observation;

  • "class_response": row, class, prior (the class's prior probability for the row) and fitted, one row per observation and class;

  • "posterior": row, the id column (when classes are assigned to groups), class (the most probable class), posterior (its probability) and probability_class_1, probability_class_2 and so on, one row per observation;

  • "probabilities": row, class, category and probability, one row per observation, class and category.

Growth mixture:

  • "response" and "conditional": row and fitted, one row per observation;

  • "class_response": row, class, prior and fitted, one row per observation and class;

  • "class_conditional": row, class, posterior (the person's posterior probability of the class) and fitted, one row per observation and class;

  • "posterior": the id column, class (the most probable class), probability (its probability) and posterior_class_1, posterior_class_2 and so on, one row per person;

  • "random_effects": the id column, class, posterior and one column per random effect, one row per person and class.

simulate() returns one row per fitted row and one column per simulation, sim_1, sim_2, ...

Details

For multilpa() and multilca() models without membership covariates, it evaluates the E-step at the estimated parameters using the fitted categorical levels, centering, and missing-data rules. Applying it to the estimation data reproduces the fitted posterior probabilities for classified observations. In a two-level model, groups in newdata are treated as new groups and classified using their supplied observations. With the default drop_empty = TRUE, rows with every indicator missing retain their position but have NA for the predicted profile and its probabilities. A group is unclassified only when none of its rows has an observed indicator. Fitted rows with zero sampling weight keep their predicted profile and probabilities under either setting of drop_empty, as in get_results(x, "assignments"). New-data prediction does not apply sampling weights. These exclusions apply to classification output; density predictions retain each row's evaluated log density. For a model with a noise component, prediction supports complete rows and, under missing = "fiml", rows with every indicator missing. Partially observed rows are unsupported because the fitted noise hypervolume does not specify their marginal density. An entirely missing row has log density zero, including under the noise component.

For growth mixtures (mixture_regression(random = )), individuals and clusters in newdata are treated as new units. Class mean trajectories require only predictors; posterior class probabilities, individual trajectories, and empirical Bayes random effects also require observed outcomes. Prediction is not supported for membership-covariate or latent transition fits and raises latents_unsupported_prediction. For these fits, use get_results(x, "posteriors") to extract posterior probabilities for the estimation data.

simulate() draws new outcomes on the fitted design of a mixture regression or growth mixture: class memberships from the fitted mixing model (group classes first in a two-level model), random effects from each class's covariance, then outcomes from each row's class regression.

Conditions

latents_bad_data when newdata lacks an indicator or the id column, contains a category absent from the estimation data, contains unsupported missing values, or does not allow evaluation of the regression design. Binomial count predictions without trial counts also raise latents_bad_data; latents_bad_argument for "probabilities" outside the ordinal family; latents_unsupported_prediction for predict() on a membership-covariate fit or a latent transition fit. latents_unsupported_noise for partially observed prediction rows in a model with a noise component. A profile or class model's predict() raises latents_bad_argument for a type it does not offer and warns with latents_unused_argument for arguments it ignores, such as data = in place of newdata =. A growth mixture prediction raises latents_bad_data when newdata lacks id, the cluster column or (for the outcome-based types) the outcome, and warns with latents_unused_argument for arguments it ignores.

Examples

# Classify new observations with a fitted profile model.
profiles <- lpa(faithful, c("eruptions", "waiting"), n_profiles = 2,
                n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
predict(profiles, data.frame(eruptions = c(2, 4.5), waiting = c(55, 80)),
        type = "posterior")
#>   row profile posterior probability_profile_1 probability_profile_2
#> 1   1       2         1          3.110134e-11          1.000000e+00
#> 2   2       1         1          1.000000e+00          1.264747e-23

# The mean outcome under each class of a mixture regression.
fit <- mixture_regression(score ~ hours, data = study_hours, n_classes = 2,
                          n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
predict(fit, data.frame(hours = c(2, 10)), type = "class_response")
#>   row   class     prior   fitted
#> 1   1 class_1 0.5645888 43.49393
#> 2   2 class_1 0.5645888 80.00640
#> 3   1 class_2 0.4354112 56.52305
#> 4   2 class_2 0.4354112 62.96629
head(simulate(fit, nsim = 2, seed = 1))
#>      sim_1    sim_2
#> 1 85.96107 84.66292
#> 2 43.06356 61.01025
#> 3 57.86180 62.03635
#> 4 51.20585 72.29776
#> 5 78.31739 84.47418
#> 6 59.89100 71.01171

# Predict an individual trajectory conditional on observed scores.
growth <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, data = subset(growth_scores, student <= 60),
                             n_classes = 2, id = "student", class_level = "group",
                             random = ~ 1, n_starts = 1, seed = 1)
predict(growth, subset(growth_scores, student == 61), type = "conditional")
#>   row   fitted
#> 1   1 58.88460
#> 2   2 65.58452
#> 3   3 72.28445
#> 4   4 75.63441
